capabilities.help: Name the features this saferm ships, for a program deciding how to drive it
capabilities.name: capabilities

args.help: One or more files or directories to move into the archive
args.name: files

flags.help: Allow recursive deletion of directories and all their contents
flags.name: recursive

flags.help: Silently skip files that do not exist instead of erroring
flags.name: ignore-missing

flags.help: Prompt for confirmation before archiving each file
flags.name: interactive

flags.help: Mandatory explanation of why this deletion is happening
flags.name: description

flags.help: Record the original rm command being replaced by saferm
flags.name: command

flags.help: Attach additional metadata as key=value pairs (repeatable)
flags.name: meta

flags.help: Run git rm --cached to stage removal in the git index
flags.name: update-git-index

flags.help: What to do when a path cannot be archived: abort (stop at the first failure) or continue (archive the remaining paths, report every failure, and exit non-zero at the end). Mandatory: there is no default
flags.name: on-error

grants.name: git-index
grants.reason: a tracked file that moved into the archive must leave the git index too, or the next commit resurrects it

delete.help: Move files to the saferm archive with metadata tracking
delete.name: delete

args.help: Record UUID or numeric database ID of the archived item to inspect (resolved by shape, in this order: a 36-character hyphenated hex string is a record UUID, an all-digit string is a numeric database ID)
args.name: target

info.help: Display full metadata and context for an archived deletion
info.name: info

flags.help: Filter results to original paths matching the given glob pattern (* spans directory separators, so /home/m/* reaches any depth)
flags.name: path

flags.help: Include items that have already been restored or purged
flags.name: all

list.help: Show all items currently held in the saferm archive
list.name: list

args.help: Record UUIDs or numeric database IDs of specific items to permanently destroy (resolved by shape, in this order: a 36-character hyphenated hex string is a record UUID, an all-digit string is a numeric database ID)
args.name: targets

flags.help: Only purge items larger than this size (e.g. 100MB, 1GB)
flags.name: larger-than

flags.help: Select all archived items for permanent destruction
flags.name: all

grants.name: purge
grants.reason: purging destroys the archived content permanently; undelete cannot bring it back

purge.help: Permanently destroy archived items and free disk space
purge.name: purge

args.help: Record UUID, numeric database ID, or original file path of the item to restore (resolved by shape, in this order: a 36-character hyphenated hex string is a record UUID, an all-digit string is a numeric database ID, anything else is a path)
args.name: target

flags.help: What to do when something already exists at the restoration destination: overwrite (check the archived copy against the record, then replace what is there) or abort (refuse and change nothing). Required only when the destination is occupied; an absent destination, or the emptied original directory of an archived tree, needs no answer. There is no default
flags.name: on-conflict

flags.help: Run git add to stage the restored path in the git index
flags.name: update-git-index

flags.help: Restore to this path instead of the record's original one. Where the content actually went is written to the record, so `info` names it afterwards
flags.name: destination

grants.name: git-index
grants.reason: a restored file is staged so the working tree and the index agree again

undelete.help: Restore a previously archived file back to its original path
undelete.name: undelete

archive_dir.help: Directory where deleted files are archived. Default derives from SAFERM_HOME (an infrastructure override: unlike config values, SAFERM_HOME is NOT suppressed by --hermetic).

db_path.help: Path to the SQLite database. Default derives from SAFERM_HOME (an infrastructure override: unlike config values, SAFERM_HOME is NOT suppressed by --hermetic).

global_flags.help: Regex patterns for env vars to exclude from metadata
global_flags.name: exclude-env-patterns

forwarding.reason: framework-internal: absorbs app-defined global flag values

edit.help: Open this application's config file in the editor named by $EDITOR, falling back to vi. The parent directory and an empty config file are created first if they do not exist, so the editor always opens something. Launching the editor counts as a mutation: under --dry-run the command records the editor invocation and opens nothing.
edit.name: edit

forwarding.reason: framework-internal: absorbs app-defined global flag values

init.help: Create a starter config file listing every flag and config field the application declares, each commented with its help text, type and default value, so the file documents itself. The format follows whichever of TOML or JSON the application was built for. Refuses with an error if a config file already exists rather than overwriting it; the created path is printed on success.
init.name: init

forwarding.reason: framework-internal: absorbs app-defined global flag values

path.help: Print the absolute path to this application's config file and nothing else, so the value can be piped straight into another command. The path is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<app>/config.<toml|json> (falling back to ~/.config), or the explicit override the application was built with. Printing it does not create the file, and reports the same path whether or not one exists yet.
path.name: path

args.help: The config key to set, matching a registered flag name
args.name: key

args.help: Value to set (comma-separated for repeatable flags, use backslash to escape commas)
args.name: value

flags.help: Clear a repeatable flag by setting its value to an empty list
flags.name: clear

flags.help: Reset a key to its default value by removing it from the config file
flags.name: default

forwarding.reason: framework-internal: absorbs app-defined global flag values

set.help: Write a persistent value into the config file so it overrides a flag's declared default on every later run. The value is coerced to the flag's own type and rejected if it does not fit: repeatable flags take a comma-separated list (backslash-escape a literal comma) and are checked for duplicates, dict flags take a JSON object. Use --default to drop a key back to its default, and --clear to empty a repeatable flag.
set.name: set

flags.help: Display config values in a human-readable table format
flags.name: plain

forwarding.reason: framework-internal: absorbs app-defined global flag values

show.help: Show every flag and config field with its effective value and where that value came from, resolved through the precedence chain environment variable, then config file, then declared default. Declared infrastructure roots, handshake and connection environment variables are listed too. Choose --plain for an aligned human-readable table; the framework-owned --json yields the same information as a machine-readable object carrying each entry's type, default and help text.
show.name: show

config.help: Manage persistent configuration values stored in the config file
config.name: config
